content.name: p
children: Priya is leaving Acme. Her application permissions were easy to remove, but one legacy table still belongs to her. PostgreSQL refuses the simple

children.name: code
children: DROP ROLE
—and that is the clue you need.

content.name: h2
children: Encode the retirement, not just the absence

content.name: p
children: Remove Priya's external role definition from chapter 5's policy and add this retirement. Retain the other roles, grants, memberships, and default privileges. The retirement declares how pgroles can remove her safely:

content.name: Fence
children:
retirements:
  - role: priya
    reassign_owned_to: app_owner
    drop_owned: true
    terminate_sessions: true

content.name: p
children: pgroles inspects dependencies before applying a drop. The generated sequence can terminate other sessions, reassign owned objects, remove remaining privileges, and finally drop the role. Review this plan carefully: role retirement is deliberately destructive.

content.name: p
children: Roles are cluster-wide, but cleanup must account for dependencies in every database. Repeat the necessary reassignment and privilege cleanup in each affected database before the final

children.name: code
children: DROP ROLE

content.name: p
children: Reassign objects you intend to preserve before running

children.name: code
children: DROP OWNED

children.name: code
children: DROP OWNED
can delete objects still owned by the retiring role; it is not merely privilege cleanup.

attributes.title: The browser cannot prove session termination

children.name: p
children: PGlite demonstrates ownership dependencies,

children.name: code
children: REASSIGN OWNED

children.name: code
children: DROP OWNED
, and

children.name: code
children: DROP ROLE
. It has no pool of authenticated concurrent sessions. In production, verify that old sessions have ended and that the identity provider can no longer authenticate the person.

children.name: strong
children: Offboarding is complete when authentication is disabled, every authorization path is gone, owned objects have a successor, and active sessions are handled.
